summary: Retain compact native latency, transaction and database SLO evidence across daemon restarts

replay.detail: No claim replay or per-request claims. Native completion paths append only in memory; checkpoint swaps the buffer under a short lock, then merges and commits outside it. Installation, checkpoints and gauge mutations publish an immutable in-memory evidence projection. Every reader, including SLO rows under caller-owned read snapshots, performs no ledger I/O. Reporting releases the request Meter before attaching budgets. Failed checkpoint counts remain available for retry alongside new completions.

schema.detail: Adds an isolated host-owned SQLite native SLO ledger with versioned minute-receipt and sampled-gauge tables. Receipts retain 30 days; gauge samples retain 30 days plus a two-hour predecessor allowance. Measurement boundaries are part of stream identity, preventing changed thresholds from reinterpreting historical bad counters.

rules.detail: Admission, transaction execution and existing p99/max diagnostic measurements are unchanged. Allowances and response policy remain in objective declarations, not in the evidence producer.

compatibility.detail: Native evidence reports expose eligible, bad, good, covered/unknown time and exact UTC cuts for 30d, 6h, 2h, 1h, 30m and 5m windows. Read transactions, write transactions and writer holds remain independent populations. Missing or interrupted minutes are unknown; no historical request volume is reconstructed. Hourly database observations hold at most two hours, and absent growth evidence cannot establish healthy capacity; a known excessive live size still proves bad time.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon rollout. The restart's partial minute and periods without committed receipts remain unknown; historical coverage accumulates only from actual retained evidence. Projection as-of time and coverage are explicit. Once the current closed-minute accounting cut advances beyond the published projection, readers expose stale/unknown evidence instead of an old green. All ledger mutation paths use one publish/invalidate boundary, including prerequisite gauge SELECT and INSERT operations: any database or summary failure invalidates healthy same-cut evidence without advancing freshness. This is a maintained projection, not a reader-triggered TTL cache.

manual.detail: The daemon initializes its host-local evidence path and checkpoints the ledger from its existing minute task.

recovery.detail: Ordinary binary rollback ignores the isolated ledger. Restoring the new binary resumes retained evidence; missing intervals are never backfilled as healthy.
